findings.claim: New in 70199b59; the learner-facing side of sme-fcc-w1. 70199b59 changed the control branch at verify-learner-test.mjs line 68 to choose the no-runnable message whenever the control run has no failed and no passed assertion. That also catches a control run whose learner test file failed to load: Vitest's JSON report then has one test file with status failed and an error message but no assertion results, so 'failed' is false and 'passed' is 0. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 70199b59, with the private overlay copied over the starter and my own learner tests written in scratch. I wrote a correct learner test that also throws at module level only when the imported default export is not the learner's own component, so it loads in the normal run and fails to load under the mutation config. The normal run showed 'Test Files 8 passed (8)' and 'Tests 8 passed (8)', and npm test then printed 'no runnable test was found in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx. The file may be missing or empty, or hold only todo or skipped tests' and exited 1. The file exists, is not empty and has just passed. Running the control directly gave numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 0 and the thrown message in testResults[0].message; a deleted file gives numTotalTestSuites 0 and an empty testResults, so the two cases can be told apart. With the c68e4995 verifier swapped into scratch, the same file got the unchanged-copy message, which was closer for this learner-made case. The more likely trigger is on the harness side: when I added a module-level throw to a scratch copy of task8-variant.jsx (restored afterwards, sha256 checked), a correct test got the same no-runnable message. A variant or plugin load failure on a platform that has never been run (Windows and Linux are unverified) would therefore tell a learner with a finished test that their file may be missing or empty, and Vitest's own error is never printed. The verdict stays exit 1 and no weak test can be accepted this way; only the diagnosis is wrong. A Vitest configuration crash is not affected: with an invalid variant the run wrote no JSON, and the existing 'could not read the test results' path, which prints Vitest's output, still applies. For a learner, the message points at the wrong thing: it asks them to write a test that already exists and passes, with no hint that the check itself could not load it.
findings.recommendation: Take the no-runnable branch only when no test file in the control report has status failed (or when the report has zero test suites), and otherwise report the load error, ideally with the failed file's message, as the 'could not read the test results' path already does with Vitest's output. Trialled in scratch on 70199b59: adding a per-run flag for any failed test file and requiring it to be false in the line-68 condition kept the deleted-file, todo-only and skip-only messages, gave the module-level load error the unchanged-copy message again, and still accepted my correct test with exit 0. Printing the suite message was not trialled. Add a module-level load error to the private adversarial controls. Low on its own; it does not justify a further correction loop unless Firstmate decides otherwise. Consolidate with sme-fcc-w1.
